source.title: Can We Scale Transformers to Predict Parameters of Diverse ImageNet Models?
source.authors: Boris Knyazev; Doha Hwang; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: Text is largely complete, with some garbled OCR and figure/table layout; no major cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training accuracy during ImageNet training from several initializations, but does not test any listed version’s specific benchmark, architecture, or initialization conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet training-accuracy curves for ResNet-50, ResNet-152 and Swin-T under several initializations (Figure 8). These are figure-only results and do not report CIFAR training error, corrupted or random labels, or the listed versions’ specific interventions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates learned parameter prediction as an initialization method. Its comparisons report initialization-method performance, without testing activation-matched initialization in plain networks, depth degradation, zero training error, stability thresholds, or a controlled batch-normalization intervention. Including Fixup as a baseline within normalization-free ResNet-50 does not establish its claimed speed and stability relative to normalized training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. GHN-3 improves early convergence and predicted-parameter quality. Final 90-epoch validation accuracies are generally similar to random initialization, with a higher Swin-T result (76.4% versus 75.6%). The authors also acknowledge architecture distribution shifts and that reaching state-of-the-art final performance generally requires about the same training duration.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates data-driven parameter prediction as an initialization method, then fine-tunes the initialized networks; it does not test the listed recipes for zero training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization method and learning rate affect reported accuracy; the paper also reports architecture distribution shift for ViT and EfficientNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 presents training-accuracy trajectories for four initialization methods on ImageNet ResNet-50, ResNet-152 and Swin-T; numerical trajectories cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random, GradInit and learned GHN initializations can produce different training trajectories in these ImageNet models.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 16 reports one-epoch ImageNet accuracy for normalization-free ResNet-50: random 10.8%, GradInit 19.2%, Fixup 18.0%, GHN-2 5.9%, and GHN-3 31.7%. This compares initialization methods within normalization-free training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization method affects early ImageNet accuracy in normalization-free ResNet-50.

record.problems: The relevant training-accuracy results appear only as curves without tabulated values or a text description. Most reported numeric comparisons are validation accuracy rather than training error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping and regularization effects. Few-shot CIFAR transfer accuracies are evaluation performance.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization enabling very deep plain tanh training.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signal and gradient propagation in plain networks, trainable depth, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons in very deep tanh networks.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes and edge-of-stability dynamics.

Controlled effects of adding batch normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched comparisons establishing Fixup's speed and stability relative to normalized residual training.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. None-linked rows are descriptive method comparisons, not evidence for verdicts on these versions. Their cannot_determine states reflect unavailable curve values, not absent effects. Tables 6 and 16 do not document a matched normalization ablation sufficient to infer a V6 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the listed model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima and teacher/student width comparisons.
Plain versus residual shortcut networks, depth-related training error, and the stated special-initialization and normalization-free conditions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss and curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization’s effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.
